params.why: arc CD must be smaller than arc BCD = 2a

stem: $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral (its vertices are in this order on the circle) in which $\overline{AB}$ is a diameter, $m(\angle DAB) = {=a}^\circ$ and $m(\widehat{CD}) = {=c}^\circ$. Find $m(\angle ADC)$ in degrees.
solution: $\overline{AB}$ is a diameter, so the angle $\angle ADB$ in the semicircle is $90^\circ$.
$\angle CBD$ is inscribed in arc $CD$, so $m(\angle CBD) = \frac{1}{2} \times {=c}^\circ = {=h}^\circ$.
$\angle B$ and $\angle D$ are opposite angles of the cyclic quadrilateral, so they are supplementary.
notes: Modelled on bk-drill-2-c (diameter, arc CD, find all angles), asking only for angle D. Text-only description; consistent configuration requires c < 2a (arc BC>0). Answers are whole numbers.
